learningObjective: Identify what semantic preservation guarantees a compiler optimization must uphold and where common flags relax it.
stem: Which statements about semantic preservation in compiler optimization are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: An optimization is semantics-preserving if the optimized program has an observable-behavior set that is a subset of the source program's observable-behavior set (under the source language's semantics), typically allowing implementation-defined behaviors and some nondeterminism.

Flags like `-ffast-math` explicitly relax IEEE-754 semantics (associativity, NaN/Inf handling), allowing reassociation and other transformations that are not strictly semantics-preserving; using them may change numerical results.

For undefined behavior (UB) in the source language (e.g., signed overflow in C, out-of-bounds access), the compiler is free to assume UB does not occur; optimizations may exploit this to eliminate branches or code paths, which can produce surprising behavior when UB does occur.
Semantic preservation is always trivially satisfied by any optimization that reduces the number of instructions; fewer instructions cannot possibly change behavior.

explanation: A: standard framing of semantic preservation as behavior refinement. B: canonical example of an intentional soundness relaxation for FP arithmetic. C: UB-based optimization is a known pattern in C/C++ that can surprise users. D is wrong: reducing instructions does not guarantee behavior preservation (removing a store can change observed memory; removing a call can skip side effects).

optionExplanations.A: Correct: canonical definition of semantics-preserving optimization.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: -ffast-math and similar flags explicitly relax FP semantics.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: UB assumptions enable aggressive optimizations that can surprise developers.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: fewer instructions can absolutely change behavior (dropping stores, calls, exceptions).

assumptions: Standard C/C++ semantics with defined observable behavior; language variants with different semantic models may allow different optimizations.
nonImplications: Does not imply -ffast-math is unsafe in all contexts; deep-learning training routinely uses it or its GPU equivalents.
Does not imply the compiler always warns when UB is assumed; it typically does not.

distractorRationales.D: Falsely claims instruction reduction implies behavior preservation.

sourceRefs.locator: Fast-math flags, UB semantics, poison values
